_about: The four standard warning letter templates every subdivision starts with (one per warning level). Seed data, not application code: each subdivision gets its OWN copy as ordinary rows (warning_letter_templates + version 1), which its Leader edits in the template editor or replaces from a DOCX; nothing here is read again after that. No fines, no Barangay steps, no enforcement powers the subdivision has not written itself. Placeholders must be keys of PLACEHOLDER_DEFINITIONS (services/warning_letters.py).

templates.name: Notice Letter
templates.description: A courteous first notice of a recorded concern. It asks for a change and states no consequence.
templates.body_template:
Dear {{resident_name}},

This is a Notice from the Office of the Subdivision Leader of {{subdivision_name}}. It is a courteous first notice about a concern recorded under case {{case_reference}}. It is not a penalty.

On {{incident_date}}, an incident involving {{pet_name}} ({{pet_type}}) was reported to the subdivision, and the Office of the Subdivision Leader verified it.

What Was Reported
{{violation_description}}

Subdivision Policy
{{policy_reference}}

What We Ask You To Do
{{required_action}}

We hope this can be settled between neighbors. If you believe this notice is mistaken, or you would like to explain what happened, please contact the Office of the Subdivision Leader and mention reference {{warning_reference}}.

This notice was issued on {{issue_date}}.

templates.name: First Warning Letter
templates.description: A formal first warning for a verified violation of a subdivision policy.
templates.body_template:
Dear {{resident_name}},

This is a formal First Warning from the Office of the Subdivision Leader of {{subdivision_name}}, issued under case {{case_reference}}.

On {{incident_date}}, an incident involving {{pet_name}} ({{pet_type}}), an animal in your care, was reported and verified as a violation of the subdivision policy below.

Violation Details
{{violation_description}}

Subdivision Policy
{{policy_reference}}

Required Corrective Action
{{required_action}}

Please carry out the corrective action above. A further violation of the same policy may lead to a Second Warning. If you wish to respond, or believe this warning was issued in error, contact the Office of the Subdivision Leader and mention reference {{warning_reference}}.

This warning was issued on {{issue_date}}.

templates.name: Second Warning Letter (with Office Summons)
templates.description: A formal second warning that follows an earlier warning, with the date and place of a meeting at the subdivision office.

templates.name: Final Notice / Escalation Letter
templates.description: The last warning level. It states that the subdivision will consider further steps under its own rules. It imposes no penalty itself.
templates.body_template:
Dear {{resident_name}},

This is a Final Notice from the Office of the Subdivision Leader of {{subdivision_name}}, issued under case {{case_reference}}. It is the last warning level in the subdivision's process.

On {{incident_date}}, a further incident involving {{pet_name}} ({{pet_type}}), an animal in your care, was reported and verified as a violation of the subdivision policy below, after earlier warnings.

Violation Details
{{violation_description}}

Subdivision Policy
{{policy_reference}}

Required Corrective Action
{{required_action}}

If this matter is not resolved, the Subdivision Leader will consider the further steps that the subdivision's own rules allow. This letter does not by itself impose any penalty. To respond, or to ask what happens next, contact the Office of the Subdivision Leader and mention reference {{warning_reference}}.

This notice was issued on {{issue_date}}.
